problem:
Evaluate the double integral
${∬}_{D}\frac{1}{(1+x+y)^{2}}\,dA,$
where $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the line
$y=1-x$ and the coordinate axes.

activity_context.topic_title: Double Integrals Over Type I Regions

feedback.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type I region.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/2}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1/x}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}}\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}[{\int }_{x}^{1/x}y\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{x}^{1/x}dx \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}-{x}^{2})dx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1/2}^{1}(\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}-1)\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1/2}^{1}(\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}-1)\,dx & =\frac{1}{2}{[-\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}}-x]}_{1/2}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}[\frac{1}{3}+1-(\frac{8}{3}+\frac{1}{2})] \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{11}{6}) \\  & =\frac{11}{12}\end{aligned}
$$
